raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I'm 60, been working this land for 40 years, so I know what grows and what doesn't. Seven mu isn't much — with seven mouths at home it means every mu has to earn its keep. Some of my kids work in town now, so I mostly have me, the wife, and whoever's around at busy times. That shapes how I plan.

**How I split the 7 mu**

Most of my land — about 4 mu — goes to the wheat-maize rotation. That's the bread and butter, literally. You can't really skip it in Quzhou. I put 1.5 mu into cotton because the soil on that western piece doesn't do as well for grain, and cotton still brings in cash even if prices aren't great. The last 1.5 mu goes to watermelon — that's my money crop. Watermelon is risky but if the season is good and I hit the early market, it pays more than everything else combined. My neighbor Old Wang did well with watermelon last two years, and I learned the trick of mulch film from him.

**Wheat (about 4 mu)**

I sow around October 10-15, Jimai 22 variety — same seed I've used, I save some and buy fresh every two-three years. Before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind), that gives me base N, P, and K in one go. Then at jointing in early March I topdress urea, maybe 15 kg/mu. Total N comes to around 16-17 kg/mu. The extension guy last spring said 18 was right for my yield level but I usually do a little less — don't want to waste money if the spring is dry. I irrigate before winter (December) and once at jointing, sometimes again at heading if it's a dry spring. Yield I expect around 450 kg/mu — last year I got 470, year before 420, so somewhere in there.

**Maize (about 4 mu, same fields as wheat)**

Tight turnaround — I hire the combine for wheat, then have maybe 4-5 days to plant maize. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has in stock, direct seeding right into the stubble. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 30 kg/mu, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, 15 kg/mu. Total N around 15 kg/mu. Usually I don't need to irrigate if the summer rains come, but I'll run the pump once or twice at tasseling if it's dry. Expect 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (1.5 mu)**

Plant late April after the soil warms, local variety I've been using for years. Cotton needs less N than maize but more patience — I put down 25 kg compound at planting, topdress 10 kg urea at squaring, maybe another 5 kg at flowering. Total N around 12 kg/mu. Irrigate 2-3 times depending on rain. Have to spray — cotton bollworm is always a problem, probably 3-4 sprays through the season. Yield maybe 250 kg/mu of seed cotton. Picking takes a lot of time, mostly me and the wife doing it by hand in September-October.

**Watermelon (1.5 mu)**

This is where I spend most of my cash on inputs. Plant mid-April under mulch film to get early to market. I use hybrid seed, about 50 yuan/mu for seed alone. Heavy on base fertilizer — around 30 kg compound plus manure from the neighbor who keeps pigs. Then I fertigate a few times through the season, maybe 8-10 kg urea equivalent per mu total, plus potash. Irrigation is critical — I irrigate 4-5 times. Sprays for aphids and fusarium, maybe 3-4 times. Yield target 2500-3000 kg/mu if the season is good. My daughter-in-law helps during harvest in July because the window is short.

**Overall thinking**

Total input cost around 4,500-5,000 yuan for the year. Most of that is watermelon and the fertilizer bill. I'm careful because I don't have savings to fall back on if something goes wrong — that's why I keep the wheat-maize steady. The watermelon is my upside but if it fails I can still eat from the grain.
